name: PLUMB CRAZY
clue: The Latin name of this heavy metal gave us the word 'plumber', since Romans made water pipes from it

name: HOLY BUBBLY
clue: Moët & Chandon's prestige cuvée honors this Benedictine monk, often but wrongly said to have invented champagne

name: MUDDY WATERS, HIGH RISES
clue: Its name means 'muddy confluence' in Malay, and its twin Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004

name: THE NAME HE HATED
clue: Charles Schulz pitched it as 'Li'l Folks' and never liked the title his syndicate gave this strip about Charlie Brown and his dog

name: HAVING THE LAST WORD
clue: Hera cursed this nymph to repeat only the final words of others, and she wasted away pining for Narcissus

name: SEA LEVEL, NOT
clue: Fossils of ancient sea creatures are locked in the limestone that forms the very top of this peak

name: OFF THE BOARDWALK
clue: Of the classic Monopoly board's colored properties, only the misspelled Marvin Gardens lies outside this New Jersey resort

name: WHAT'S UP, MAESTRO?
clue: Elmer Fudd sings 'Kill the wabbit!' to the 'Ride of the Valkyries' by this composer in a 1957 Chuck Jones cartoon

name: AN ILL WIND FOR KUBLAI
clue: Japanese for 'divine wind', this word was given to the typhoons said to have wrecked two Mongol invasion fleets in the 1200s

name: RUNNING MATE TROUBLE
clue: His electoral tie with his own running mate, Thomas Jefferson, sent the 1800 election to the House and led to the 12th Amendment

name: WHY IT'S IN PARIS
clue: Leonardo took this portrait with him when he moved to France late in life, and it ended up with a French king

name: K, THE BOOKENDS
clue: George Eastman coined this brand name in 1888, starting and ending it with K, a letter he found strong and incisive

name: SPLIT PERSONALITY
clue: Greek thinkers named this for being uncuttable, a label that 20th-century physics proved wrong

name: COACH CLASS
clue: The University of Kansas's first basketball coach posted a losing record there, though he had invented the game

name: TOP ROW SEATS
clue: Typists still use this layout, named for letters on the top row of Christopher Sholes's 1870s typewriters

name: BROKEN AND MENDED
clue: This branch of math takes its name from 'al-jabr', Arabic for 'restoration', in a 9th-century book title

name: BRANCHING OUT
clue: Flanked by two olive branches, a seven-branched one of these lampstands appears on Israel's official emblem

name: RING LEADER
clue: Pierre de Coubertin said its five colors on a white field reproduced the colors of every nation's banner

name: BACK TO THE PLOW
clue: This Ohio city takes its name from a society honoring a Roman who left his farm to lead, then went right back to it

name: LAST STOP
clue: In 1910, at 82, this author of an epic of Napoleon's invasion fled his estate and died days later at a remote railway station
